hints.title: Dynamic Window with Frequency Bound
hints.text: Expand the right pointer across the string while maintaining a record of seen character counts, shrinking the left boundary whenever more than two distinct characters are present.

hints.title: Contracting Window on Excess Character Diversity
hints.text: Use a map to track frequencies in the current substring. When the map size exceeds two, decrement counts from the left until one character count drops to zero and can be removed.

hints.title: Two Pointers with Character Counter
hints.text: Initialize left pointer and maximum length at zero. For right from zero to n - 1, increment frequency of s[right]. While map size > 2, decrement count of s[left], delete key if count reaches zero, and increment left. Update max length with right - left + 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def lengthOfLongestSubstringTwoDistinct(self, s: str) -> int:
        from collections import defaultdict
        counts = defaultdict(int)
        left = 0
        max_len = 0
        for right in range(len(s)):
            counts[s[right]] += 1
            while len(counts) > 2:
                counts[s[left]] -= 1
                if counts[s[left]] == 0:
                    del counts[s[left]]
                left += 1
            max_len = max(max_len, right - left + 1)
        return max_len
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving linear O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space since at most 3 distinct characters exist in the frequency map at any time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all substrings takes cubic or quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A sliding window ensures each character is visited at most twice (once by right, once by left).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should know how to remove entries from the frequency map when their count reaches zero to keep map size accurate.
